rows.label: Deaths per DALY attributable to bacterial antimicrobial resistance (GRAM, 2021)

source.title: GBD 2021 Antimicrobial Resistance Collaborators, Global burden of bacterial antimicrobial resistance 1990–2021 (Lancet 2024)
source.quote: The global number of DALYs attributable to AMR decreased between 1990 (60·9 million [95% UI 47·7–74·1]) and 2021 (42·6 million [36·1–49·0])
source.note: 1.14 million deaths attributable to AMR in 2021 over 42.6 million attributable DALYs: 37.4 DALYs per death.

rows.explainer: Turns the AMR DALYs in Ambitious Impact's antibiotics model (ARMoR) back into deaths, so each can be valued by age.

rows.label: Share of AMR-attributable deaths under age 5 (GRAM 2021)

source.title: GBD 2021 Antimicrobial Resistance Collaborators, Global burden of bacterial antimicrobial resistance 1990–2021 (Lancet 2024)
source.quote: For children younger than 5 years in 2021, there were 193 000 deaths (144 000–242 000) attributable to AMR globally
source.note: Under 5: 193,000 of 1.14 million attributable deaths (17%). The paper gives no world split above five; 70 and over make up 65.9% of attributable deaths in its 2050 forecast and 83.9% in high-income Asia Pacific in 2021. The split of the 83% at five and older is our judgment: 2% at 5–14, 14% at 15–49, 67% at 50 and older.

rows.explainer: Ages of the deaths antimicrobial resistance causes, for ARMoR's model: under five from GRAM 2021; the split above five is our judgment from GRAM's regional and 2050 shares (the policy's benefits come years from now, when more of these deaths are of older people).

rows.label: Deaths per DALY from childhood cancer, ages 0-19 (GBD 2023, world)

source.title: Force et al. (GBD 2023 Childhood Cancer Collaborators), Global burden of cancer in children and adolescents aged 0-19 years, 1990-2023, The Lancet 2026
source.quote: 377 000 incident childhood cancer cases (95% UI 288 000-489 000), 144 000 deaths (131 000-162 000), and 11·7 million (10·7-13·2) DALYs due to childhood cancer

rows.explainer: 144,000 deaths over 11.7 million DALYs, 81 DALYs per death (nearly all of them years of life lost at GBD's standard life expectancy): turns childhood cancer DALYs back into deaths, so each can be valued by age. rows.explainer: Our judgment, for medicines and health spending at the margin in low- and middle-income countries (charityevals' Direct Relief model): in the Global Burden of Disease, years lived with disability are about a third of all DALYs worldwide, less where child deaths dominate and more where chronic illness does (Ukraine, the Middle East). 40%, from 25% to 55%. The rest are deaths, valued by age.

rows.label: Deaths per DALY of years of life lost, deaths averted by medicines in low- and middle-income countries
rows.explainer: Our judgment: about 30 years of life lost per death (20 to 45), between the GBD's 22.8 DALYs per cardiovascular death worldwide (cvd_deaths_per_daly_world) and its 37 per antimicrobial-resistance death (amr_deaths_per_daly), with child deaths (about 88 years each) a minority of those these medicines avert. Turns years of life lost back into deaths, valued by age.

rows.label: Crises: of the deaths at five or older, share aged 5 to 14 (judgment, shared by the relief models)
rows.explainer: Judgment 20% (10-40%): in crisis mortality surveys most deaths over five are of adults, and children of 5-14 are about a quarter to a third of displaced populations but die at a far lower rate than under-fives or older adults. The relief models' one figure for the rest of the age split after under-fives, where no WHO or GBD split for the crisis exists (the family guide, humanitarian-relief.md); read by every model that would otherwise type it.

rows.label: COVID-scale pandemic: share of the deaths that are of children under five
rows.explainer: COVID-19's excess deaths were mostly of older people and few of young children; a different pathogen could hit children harder (the range's top). Anchored on WHO's excess-mortality age profile (Msemburi et al. 2023, Nature: most excess deaths over 60). Our judgment, read by every model that counts a COVID-scale pandemic averted.

rows.label: COVID-scale pandemic: of the deaths at five or older, share aged 5 to 14
rows.explainer: School-age children were the least affected group in COVID-19; up to 5% for a pathogen like the 1918 influenza. Our judgment, read by every model that counts a COVID-scale pandemic averted.

rows.label: COVID-scale pandemic: of the deaths at 15 or older, share aged 15 to 49
rows.explainer: About 15% of COVID-19's adult excess deaths were under 50 (WHO's age profile, most deaths over 60); up to 40% for a pathogen that kills young adults (1918 influenza). The rest are valued at the 50-74 band. Our judgment, read by every model that counts a COVID-scale pandemic averted.
